Advice to Students:

Attend every class!!! Missing even one class can have a substantial effect on your ability to understand the course. Be prepared to think and concentrate, in the class and outside. I will try to make the class very interactive. Participate in the class discussions. Ask questions when you don’t understand something. Keep up with the class readings. Start assignments and homework early. Meet me in office hour to discuss ideas, solutions or to check if, what you understand is correct.

Collaboration Policy:

We encourage discussion between students regarding the course material. However, no discussion of any sort is allowed with anyone on the assignment and homework for the class. If you find solution to some problems in a book or on the internet, you may use their idea for the solution; provided you acknowledge the source (name and page in the book or the website, if the idea is found on the internet). Even though you are allowed to use ideas from another source, you must write the solution in your own words. If you are unsure whether or not certain kinds of collaboration is possible, please ask the teacher.

* Recommended distribution: - 30 Marks from Assignments, 40 marks based on assignments with slightly enhance difficulty /complex, 30 marks from thought provoking

Learning Outcomes: The Learner will:Assessment Criteria: The Learner can:Evaluated under ISA/MSE/ESE/LAB
Explain the concept of e-waste, identify hazardous substances in electronic waste, and analyze their impacts on human health and the environment.- Define e-waste and list examples of electronic waste. - Identify hazardous components (e.g., lead, mercury, cadmium). - Analyze and describe their effects on human organs and ecological systems.ISA
Assess domestic e-waste disposal practices and explore effective strategies for sustainable e-waste management.- List common disposal methods used in households. - Evaluate their environmental implications. - Propose alternative sustainable practices (e.g., extended producer responsibility).ISA
Describe technologies for resource recovery from e-waste and summarize guidelines for the environmentally sound management of electronic waste.- Explain technologies like hydrometallurgy, pyrometallurgy, and biometallurgy. - Summarize CPCB/UNEP guidelines for safe disposal. - Distinguish between compliant and non-compliant recycling methods.ISA
Analyze the occupational and environmental health challenges associated with e-waste recycling in India and propose measures to mitigate these risks.- Identify unorganized sector practices in India. - Assess exposure risks for workers and communities. - Suggest engineering, legal, and educational mitigation strategies.ISA
Describe the technologies used for the recovery of resources and materials from e-waste, focusing on mechanical processing and advanced recovery methods.- Describe steps in mechanical shredding, sorting, and refining. - Differentiate mechanical and chemical processes. - Identify recovery rates and efficiency.ISA
Assess the resource recovery potential of e-waste, including valuable metals and other materials, and understand its significance for sustainable resource management.- List valuable recoverable materials (e.g., gold, copper, palladium). - Estimate recovery potential in given samples. - Link recovery to circular economy and sustainability.ISA
Explain the step-by-step process of e-waste recycling and material recovery, highlighting the role of different technologies in efficient resource extraction.- Create a flowchart of the e-waste recycling process. - Explain roles of different equipment (e.g., crushers, eddy current separators). - Identify loss points and recommend optimizations.ISA
Explain the exposure pathways of pollutants emitted during e-waste recycling and their effects on environmental and public health. - Define key pollutants released during informal recycling. - Identify air, soil, and water exposure pathways. - Assess long-term public health risks using case data.ISA
Conduct a health risk assessment related to e-waste recycling, identifying key risks and proposing strategies to minimize adverse health impacts.- List exposure pathways and calculate dose estimates. - Identify critical health endpoints (e.g., neurotoxicity, respiratory illness). - Propose PPE usage, medical surveillance, and policy changes.ISA
Explain the evolution and salient features of Indian e-waste management rules (2011 and 2016), the Hazardous Waste Rules (2008), and the government’s assistance for Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs).- State timeline and milestones in e-waste law development. - Highlight key changes in 2016 rules (e.g., PROs, EPR). - Describe TSDF model and support mechanisms.ISA
Compare international e-waste management legislation, including the Basel, Bamako, and Rotterdam Conventions, and directives such as WEEE and RoHS, highlighting their implications for sustainable e-waste practices.- Summarize the scope and objective of each convention. - Create a comparison matrix for compliance requirements. - Analyze India's obligations under Basel Convention.ISA
Assess case studies and unique e-waste management initiatives from around the world, identifying best practices and their potential applicability in different contexts.- Identify at least three case studies (e.g., Japan, EU, Rwanda). - Describe the model followed in each. - Evaluate scalability in Indian context.ISA
Explain the concept of green buildings and identify various indoor air pollutants along with their health impacts.- Define green building and key parameters (e.g., energy, water use). - List common indoor pollutants (e.g., VOCs, formaldehyde). - Describe associated health symptoms and mitigation.ISA
Describe the concept of carbon credit and evaluate disaster management techniques to mitigate the impacts of earthquakes and floods.- Explain carbon credit trading and GHG mitigation. - Describe structural/non-structural disaster preparedness methods. - Propose disaster-resilient tech solutions.ISA
Understand the basics of remote sensing and GIS and analyze their applications in addressing environmental challenges.- Define RS and GIS with examples. - Demonstrate mapping of landfill or contaminated sites. - Explain use in flood prediction or forest cover analysis.ISA
Explain the concept and significance of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), environmental audits, eco-labeling, and relevant ISO standards (14001, 18001, and 31001).- Describe EIA process steps and legal mandate. - List key indicators for eco-audit and ISO certifications. - Identify products that carry eco-labels.ISA
Describe the functions and powers of the Central and State Pollution Control Boards in enforcing pollution control legislation.- List roles such as issuing consent, enforcing law, monitoring quality. - Differentiate CPCB and SPCB functions. - Explain how boards ensure compliance.ISA
Understand the processes involved in obtaining environmental clearance, consent, and authorization, and their role in ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.- Describe steps in environmental clearance process. - Fill sample consent forms or mock applications. - Justify the importance of each approval in project cycles.ISA
